question: A large plant applies free chlorine ahead of its clearwell and chloramine in the distribution system. Why does the strategy assign the two disinfectants different roles?
correctAnswer: Free chlorine gives rapid inactivation in the plant, and chloramine gives a longer lasting residual in the system
explanation: Free chlorine inactivates organisms quickly during plant contact, while chloramine decays more slowly and helps hold a residual through the distribution system.
options: Free chlorine gives rapid inactivation in the plant, and chloramine gives a longer lasting residual in the system
Free chlorine gives a longer lasting residual in the system, and chloramine gives rapid inactivation in the plant
Free chlorine removes turbidity in the plant, and chloramine removes dissolved metals in the distribution system
Free chlorine raises alkalinity in the plant, and chloramine lowers water age in the distribution system pipes

optionB: Free chlorine gives a longer lasting residual in the system, and chloramine gives rapid inactivation in the plant
optionC: Free chlorine removes turbidity in the plant, and chloramine removes dissolved metals in the distribution system
optionD: Free chlorine raises alkalinity in the plant, and chloramine lowers water age in the distribution system pipes

question: An operator calculates a CT value for a chlorine contact basin. Which two measured inputs are multiplied to produce that value?
correctAnswer: Residual concentration in mg/L and contact time in minutes
explanation: CT is the residual disinfectant concentration, in mg/L, multiplied by the effective contact time, in minutes. Temperature and pH affect the CT that is required, not the CT that is achieved.
options: Raw water flow in L/s and basin depth in metres of water
Chlorine dose in mg/L and clearwell volume in cubic metres
Residual concentration in mg/L and contact time in minutes
Water temperature in degrees and chlorine demand in mg/L

optionB: Chlorine dose in mg/L and clearwell volume in cubic metres

optionD: Water temperature in degrees and chlorine demand in mg/L

question: A chlorine basin runs at a steady residual of 0.8 mg/L. One of two identical basins is drained for repair, cutting the effective contact time in half. What happens to the achieved CT?

explanation: CT equals residual multiplied by contact time, so halving the time at the same residual halves the achieved CT. Faster movement through the basin is exactly why the time component drops.
options: It stays the same because the residual concentration is unchanged
It doubles because the same flow passes through a smaller volume
It falls to about half because contact time is one of its two factors
It rises slightly because the water moves through the basin faster

Order a larger lagoon liner so the extra volume can be stored next season
Reduce the clarifier sludge blanket and let solids pass to the filters
Haul one load of sludge and treat the level drop as the full answer

Controlling flow with pump speed and opening the discharge valve
Running a second identical pump in parallel at the same setting

Cut the dose in one step and rely on finished turbidity alarms to catch problems

Contact basins lose volume in winter because the concrete contracts
Chlorine stops reacting entirely once water drops below 5 degrees

question: A contact basin has a theoretical detention time of 60 minutes, yet its credited contact time is much shorter. Which concept explains the gap?
correctAnswer: Tracer testing shows the effective time, often called T10, is shorter than the theoretical time
explanation: Short circuiting means part of the flow crosses the basin quickly, so tracer based effective time, the time by which 10 percent of the flow has passed, is shorter than the theoretical detention time. Credit rests on that effective time.

Chlorine decays to zero in the first few minutes of any basin, whatever its baffling
Basins are credited using the time of the slowest moving parcel of water they contain
Basins are credited using the full theoretical detention time in every design case
optionA: Tracer testing shows the effective time, often called T10, is shorter than the theoretical time

optionD: Basins are credited using the full theoretical detention time in every design case

question: A laboratory proficiency testing result for chlorine comes back outside the accepted range. Which sequence of steps is correct?

Stop all chlorine testing at the plant until the next proficiency round arrives

question: Raising the chlorine dose would fix a distribution residual problem, but the raw water carries high organic levels and byproduct results are already climbing. Which decision balances both risks?
correctAnswer: Improve precursor removal and adjust dose points so residual is held with less byproduct formation
explanation: The balanced move attacks the cause: better removal of organic precursors lets the plant hold its residual targets while forming fewer byproducts. Dose swings in either direction trade one risk for the other.
options: Raise the dose in one step and accept the byproduct trend as unavoidable
Cut the dose sharply so byproduct formation falls, whatever the residual does
Improve precursor removal and adjust dose points so residual is held with less byproduct formation
Switch the sampling sites so byproduct samples come from low organic areas
optionA: Raise the dose in one step and accept the byproduct trend as unavoidable
optionB: Cut the dose sharply so byproduct formation falls, whatever the residual does
optionC: Improve precursor removal and adjust dose points so residual is held with less byproduct formation
optionD: Switch the sampling sites so byproduct samples come from low organic areas

question: Two contact basins run in parallel, but a partly closed valve sends most flow through one basin and a trickle through the other. How is disinfection credit judged?
correctAnswer: By the lowest CT among the flow paths, since that path sets the protection level
explanation: Water taking the fast, heavily loaded path receives the least disinfection, and credit follows that weakest path rather than an average. Flow balancing is what brings the low path back up.
options: By the average CT of the two basins weighted by their volumes
By the CT of the basin carrying the smaller share of the flow
By the combined volume of both basins at the total plant flow
By the lowest CT among the flow paths, since that path sets the protection level
optionA: By the average CT of the two basins weighted by their volumes
optionB: By the CT of the basin carrying the smaller share of the flow
optionC: By the combined volume of both basins at the total plant flow
optionD: By the lowest CT among the flow paths, since that path sets the protection level

question: A plant demand charge is set by its highest 15 minute draw each month, and starting two large pumps together set that peak last month. Which change targets the charge?
correctAnswer: Stagger the large pump starts and use soft starts so the draws do not stack

Run both large pumps for longer hours so the peak is spread over the month
Move all pumping to the afternoon when the plant is fully staffed each day
Install a larger main service so the plant can draw more power at once

optionB: Run both large pumps for longer hours so the peak is spread over the month
optionC: Move all pumping to the afternoon when the plant is fully staffed each day

question: A calibration check finds a coagulant feed pump delivering about 15 percent less than its controller indicates, and the last check was 60 days ago. What assessment should follow?

Recalibrate the pump and record the new setting without reviewing the earlier period
Raise the dose by 15 percent for the next 60 days to make up the earlier shortfall

question: At a disinfection control point, the operational limit is set tighter than the critical limit. What is the operational limit for?
correctAnswer: It triggers adjustment while there is still margin before the critical limit
explanation: An operational limit is an early action trigger set inside the critical limit, so operators correct the process while a safety margin remains. The critical limit stays the boundary that must not be crossed.
options: It triggers adjustment while there is still margin before the critical limit
It replaces the critical limit in months when raw water quality is poor
It lets operators average readings across a week before taking any action
It records the highest value the process reached during the past year
